title: In-class Exercise 1: Geospatial Data Science with R
text:
2 Getting Started in R

Create a new project under File - New Project. Set up a new directory for easy navigation and launch the project.
Next, create a new folder named In-class_Ex.
Inside this folder, create a subfolder named In-class_Ex01. Then, create a new Quarto document and save it in the In-class_Ex01 subfolder. Name the file In-class_Ex01.qmd.
Usually we also create another subfolder named data for storing datasets used during the analysis. Within the data folder, create three subfolders: geospatial, aspatial (attribute table), and rds for saving different types of data.

title: In-class Exercise 1: Geospatial Data Science with R
section: 3 Installing and Loading the R packages
text:
3 Installing and Loading the R packages
There are 4 packages used in this exercise.


Package
Description



sf
Handles importing, managing, and processing vector-based geospatial data


tidyverse
A collection of R packages for data wrangling and visualisation, including readr, dplyr, and ggplot2.


tmap
Creates cartographic quality static and interactive thematic (choropleth) maps.


ggstatsplot
An extension of ggplot2.Provides graphical displays of statistical tests.



The code chunk below loads the required package into R.

pacman::p_load(tidyverse, sf, tmap, ggstatsplot)

If the required packages are not yet installed, use the function install.packages() to install them first. Remember to enclose the package names in double quotation marks (““) and separate them with commas (,) if installing more than one package.

section: 4 Working with Master Plan Planning Sub-zone Data
text:
4 Working with Master Plan Planning Sub-zone Data

As mentioned earlier, create a subfolder named data inside the In-class_Ex01 folder.
If necessary, visit data.gov.sg and download the Master Plan 2014 Subzone Boundary (Web) dataset from the portal in both the ESRI Shapefile and KML file formats.

The code chunk below imports the Master Plan 2014 Subzone Boundary (Web) dataset in both Shapefile and KML formats, and saves them as sf (simple features) data frames. Note that the import syntax differs between the two formats: when importing a Shapefile, the file extension .shp is not required, while for a KML file, the full file name including the extension must be specified in the relative directory path.

mpsz14_shp <- st_read(dsn = "data/", layer = "MP14_SUBZONE_WEB_PL")

Reading layer `MP14_SUBZONE_WEB_PL' from data source 
  `C:\lsrgc\ISSS626-yiqiong-pan\In-class_Ex\In-class_Ex01\data' 
  using driver `ESRI Shapefile'
Simple feature collection with 323 features and 15 fields
Geometry type: MULTIPOLYGON
Dimension:     XY
Bounding box:  xmin: 2667.538 ymin: 15748.72 xmax: 56396.44 ymax: 50256.33
Projected CRS: SVY21


However, we encounter error message when importing the kml file.
After receiving an error that the Web KML version cannot be opened, the code chunk below confirms that R can process KML files correctly.

st_drivers()%>% filter(grepl("KML", name))

    name                     long_name write  copy is_raster is_vector  vsi
KML  KML Keyhole Markup Language (KML)  TRUE FALSE     FALSE      TRUE TRUE


The code chunk below lists all the files in kml exension in the data folder.

list.files("data/", pattern = "\\.kml$", full.names = TRUE)

[1] "data/MasterPlan2014SubzoneBoundaryNoSeaKML.kml"
[2] "data/MasterPlan2014SubzoneBoundaryWebKML.kml"  
[3] "data/MasterPlan2019SubzoneBoundaryNoSeaKML.kml"
[4] "data/MP14_SUBZONE_WEB_PL.kml"                  
[5] "data/PreSchoolsLocation.kml"                   


We also tested another 2014 Master Plan KML (“No Sea”), but it cannot be read either.
The 2019 version loads successfully, confirming that the issue lies with the 2014 KML file format.

mpsz19_kml <- st_read("data/MasterPlan2019SubzoneBoundaryNoSeaKML.kml")

Reading layer `URA_MP19_SUBZONE_NO_SEA_PL' from data source 
  `C:\lsrgc\ISSS626-yiqiong-pan\In-class_Ex\In-class_Ex01\data\MasterPlan2019SubzoneBoundaryNoSeaKML.kml' 
  using driver `KML'
Simple feature collection with 332 features and 2 fields
Geometry type: MULTIPOLYGON
Dimension:     XY
Bounding box:  xmin: 103.6057 ymin: 1.158699 xmax: 104.0885 ymax: 1.470775
Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84


Task:
The code chunk exports mpsz14_shp sf data.frame into kml file save the output in data sub-folder and names the output file MP14_SUBZONE_WEB_PL. delete_dsn = TRUE checks if a file named MP14_SUBZONE_WEB_PL.kml already exists in the data folder, if so, it will delete it before writing a new kml file.

st_write(mpsz14_shp, 
        "data/MP14_SUBZONE_WEB_PL.kml",
        delete_dsn = TRUE)

Deleting source `data/MP14_SUBZONE_WEB_PL.kml' using driver `KML'
Writing layer `MP14_SUBZONE_WEB_PL' to data source 
  `data/MP14_SUBZONE_WEB_PL.kml' using driver `KML'
Writing 323 features with 15 fields and geometry type Multi Polygon.
